mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on both teams showing a recent-vs-all-prior possession shift in the same direction (both TEAM_A and TEAM_B show elevated RECENT_5 possession FOR vs ALL_PRIOR FOR), then jointly examine whether shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR also shift upward in RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR for the same teams. This is a joint two-team, two-observable co-movement test, not a single observable mirror.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams simultaneously show a recent possession surge, their recent shot production rises jointly above their long-run averages — the co-movement is stronger than either possession or shots alone would predict independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When a team's recent possession share (RECENT_5) diverges sharply upward from its all-prior average, its shots and shots-on-target production in the same recent window also rises disproportionately relative to its all-prior shot rate — testing whether the joint possession-surge and shot-surge co-move across both teams simultaneously in the same fixture context.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across two distinct observables (possession and shots) for both teams simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to one observable with one conditioning band; it tests whether the cross-observable co-movement is coherent across both sides at once.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the ratio of shots_on_target FOR to shots FOR (accuracy) from ALL_PRIOR data, and cross it against the opponent's shots_on_target AGAINST (allowed) rate. Condition on cases where one team's accuracy ratio is below the competition context baseline while the opponent's allowed shots_on_target is also below baseline — a two-dimensional joint suppression condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's own shot accuracy is below the competition baseline AND its opponent allows fewer shots on target than the competition baseline, the team's shots_on_target FOR is suppressed below what either dimension alone would predict — a non-additive joint suppression.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: A team's shots-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shot accuracy) interacts with its opponent's shots-on-target allowed rate: when one side has high shot volume but low on-target accuracy while the opponent allows few shots on target, the joint suppression of on-target output is greater than either observable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for one team conditioned simultaneously on two opponent-descriptor dimensions (opponent's allowed shots_on_target and the team's own accuracy ratio). It is not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the ratio of corner_kicks FOR in FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF (both ALL_PRIOR). Similarly compute corner_kicks AGAINST in FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF. Condition on the case where one team's FOR corners are back-loaded (second half > first half) and the opponent's AGAINST corners are also back-loaded — a joint within-match half-level asymmetry across both teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' half-level corner profiles are jointly back-loaded (team's own second-half FOR corners exceed first-half, and opponent's second-half AGAINST corners exceed first-half), total second-half corner volume rises above what the full-match average would imply — a non-linear within-match state dependence.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: A team's corner kick production splits asymmetrically across halves (first-half vs second-half FOR rates), and this within-match half-level asymmetry differs between the two teams — testing whether the team with a stronger second-half corner bias faces an opponent whose corner-allowed rate is also skewed toward the second half, producing a compounding second-half corner surge.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF) combined with a joint condition across both teams' FOR and AGAINST half-profiles simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one coarse band; it is a two-team, two-half asymmetry interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the direction of shift (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) for both yellow_cards FOR and fouls FOR. Condition on the case where one team shows a joint suppression in both yellow cards and fouls recently (both RECENT_5 below ALL_PRIOR) while the opponent shows a joint elevation in both — an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable disciplinary regime divergence.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's recent yellow card and foul rates are jointly suppressed while the opponent's are jointly elevated, the match-level total cards and fouls are driven asymmetrically by the elevated team, and the suppressed team's contribution is below its long-run average — the asymmetry is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: A team's recent-window (RECENT_5) yellow card rate diverging from its all-prior average, when jointly considered with its recent foul rate divergence, tests whether the two disciplinary observables co-move in the same direction (both elevated or both suppressed recently) — and whether this joint recent disciplinary regime shift is asymmetric between the two teams (one team's regime shifting while the other's does not).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric joint relationship across two distinct observables (yellow_cards and fouls) for two teams simultaneously, conditioned on the direction of recent-vs-all-prior regime shift for both observables at once. It cannot be reduced to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compare fouls FOR at HOME vs AWAY (venue split) and cross this against cards_2h FOR (second-half cards, ALL_PRIOR). Condition on the case where a team's away foul rate exceeds its home foul rate AND its second-half card rate (cards_2h) is above the competition context baseline — testing whether the venue-driven foul elevation translates into a second-half card elevation beyond what the full-match card average would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Teams whose away foul rate materially exceeds their home foul rate show a disproportionate elevation in second-half cards when playing away, above what their full-match yellow card average or the competition baseline would imply — a non-additive venue-by-foul-by-half interaction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The second-half cards (cards_2h) rate for each team, when jointly conditioned on both teams' full-match foul rates and the venue split (home vs away foul tendencies), tests whether a team that commits more fouls away from home also accumulates disproportionately more second-half cards away — an interaction between venue-conditioned foul production and within-match second-half card accumulation that requires both the venue dimension and the foul observable simultaneously.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on venue (home vs away foul split), a second distinct observable (fouls), and a within-match half-level period (second half cards). It involves two distinct observables and two conditioning dimensions (venue and half), which is structurally richer than any single-observable, single-band covered case.
